title: Penalized learning identifies a cardiomyopathy-associated cytokine pattern
summary: A LASSO-selected four-cytokine combination distinguished chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy from rheumatic heart disease in a small cross-sectional clinical study. The represented finding is a cohort-specific multivariable immune-profile association, not a verified causal inflammatory pathway or a deployable diagnostic test.
organization: Federal University of Minas Gerais; Federal University of Paraná

source_review.scope: Exact primary front and selected computational/clinical Methods and corresponding high-level Results; operational laboratory protocols excluded from review

evidence.tested: The study included 38 chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy cases, 17 rheumatic heart disease cases and 12 healthy controls. An 80:20 random split was described for LASSO logistic classification; the selected panel comprised IL-12p70, IL-7, IL-1Ra and IL-4.
evidence.unknown: A claimed 100% separation comes from a very small selected sample; the main result does not establish precision, external generalization or a robust future-patient operating threshold. Disease groups have different sex distributions, and controls were much younger. Parameter-selection nesting and test counts are incompletely specified. Conventional pairwise cytokine differences, generic networks and t-SNE visualization are separate from the enabling penalized model. No pathogen experimentation or therapeutic intervention is represented.
evidence.ai_role: Regularized fitted classification selects a joint cytokine pattern from measured clinical variables; the scoped finding concerns its observed disease-group association.
